extracted.intended_audience: pun enthusiasts, potential contestants, and general public interested in the O. Henry Pun-Off
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, formats, and judging criteria for the O. Henry Pun-Off World Championships — including the two contest types (Punniest of Show and PunSlingers), accepted forms of puns, scoring system, and awards. Useful for contestants and organizers preparing for/sampling the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punniest of Show (prepared monologue)
rubrics_metrics.description: Punniest of Show features individuals performing a 90-second prepared monologue filled with puns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format requirement: prepared material (not spontaneous); strict time guideline of 90 seconds. Participants may compete in one or both contest types (Punniest of Show and PunSlingers).

rubrics_metrics.name: PunSlingers (spontaneous head-to-head)
rubrics_metrics.description: PunSlingers pits individual punsters in head-to-head bouts of spontaneous punning on a randomly selected variation of traditional topic themes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes spontaneity and on-the-spot creativity; topics are randomly selected variations of traditional themes to prompt rapid punning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-fold definition of a proper pun
rubrics_metrics.description: For competition and judging the Pun-Off adopts a two-fold definition: (1) wordplay using homonyms that deliberately exploits ambiguity between similar-sounding words for humorous or rhetorical effect; (2) a lesser used form of euphemism or double entendre, where an alternate meaning is suggested for a word for comedic effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the accepted types of punning for entries — homonym-based wordplay and euphemistic/double-entendre constructions. Entrants should craft material falling within these forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging dimensions: performance, originality, and wit
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges offer scores based on performance, originality, and wit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three broad qualitative dimensions are the explicit bases for numerical scoring; contestants should aim to maximize delivery (performance), novel material or angles (originality), and comedic cleverness (wit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge scoring scale (1–10) and normalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges give scores of 1–10 based on performance, originality, and wit. Scores lower than 1 are raised to 1, and scores higher than 10 are lowered to 10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each judge's numeric score is constrained to the 1–10 range; the normalization rule ensures out-of-range values are adjusted to the bounds (historical note: this framing accompanies the four-person panel era).

rubrics_metrics.name: Score aggregation and panel size (4–40 combined score; six-judge discard rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Originally a four-person panel offered four scores that were added together for a combined score of 4–40. Beginning in 2009 the judge panel was expanded to six people, with the highest and lowest scores discarded and the remaining four scores added together to form each participant's combined score of 4–40.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregation yields a 4–40 combined score per participant. The six-judge discard rule was enacted to reduce the influence of any single outlier judge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of six-judge/discard rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The expansion to six judges with highest and lowest discarded was enacted to prevent any one judge from having the ability to disqualify a punster by giving a much lower score than the other judges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit procedural safeguard against judge bias or extreme scoring; organizers and contestants should be aware that extreme outlier scores are removed before summing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tie-breaking: audience applause
rubrics_metrics.description: The highest-scoring punster wins each event, with ties being decided by audience applause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the event of a tied combined score, the audience's reaction (applause) determines the winner — audience engagement can thus be decisive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most Viable Punster (peer-voted award)
rubrics_metrics.description: A separate award given yearly for the Most Viable Punster, a title awarded by votes from each year's participants and given in honor of late punster George McClughan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a peer-choice award distinct from the judge-scored events; it is determined by contestant votes rather than judge scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration timing and contestant slots
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration for the Pun-Off opens each year on April Fool's Day, and contestant slots can fill up quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural guidance for prospective contestants: register promptly when registration opens to secure a slot; historically contestants come from local to international locations.
